bug_semantics: When persistent proxy memory is enabled, the proxy used the client-controlled x-headroom-user-id header verbatim as the memory partition key. That value flowed into search_memories and save/update/delete operations and into context/tool handling, without authentication or any binding between the selected partition and the caller. A client able to reach a data-plane route could therefore choose another user's identifier, retrieve that user's stored LLM memory through context/search, and write or alter memory in that partition. The flaw began on the original Anthropic memory-enabled proxy path, was later copied to OpenAI Chat Completions, Gemini, OpenAI Responses, and OpenAI websocket paths, and was practically network-reachable in the reference compose deployment because it bound the proxy to 0.0.0.0 and published port 8787 without requiring HEADROOM_PROXY_TOKEN. Fix 1f96dabc19130947770353cd6e814db4fd96e6a0 centralizes identity selection in resolve_memory_identity: the header is honored only for a loopback peer (or by a deployment-supplied authenticated resolver); a remote peer instead gets the configured proxy-token fingerprint or OS-user fallback. The same fix requires a proxy token in the shipped compose file.
flaw_origin: The smallest public-history BIC is da743418584725e8b9c3315dc1aea7cf5e949192, not the April OpenAI handler additions or the later handler split/refactors. This one-parent commit introduced the persistent memory proxy integration itself. In headroom/proxy/server.py it added memory_user_id = headers.get("x-headroom-user-id"), required only that the caller supply a nonempty value, then passed that untrusted value to MemoryHandler.search_and_format_context and MemoryHandler.handle_memory_tool_calls. The same commit created headroom/proxy/memory_handler.py, where the user_id argument directly scopes backend search_memories and save_memory operations. Parent 8c22a72715a328f1f7c3d4ba4a44516910192e80 has neither the header read nor the proxy memory handler. Commit e8ab444f09e981343c2a77ce88ef7725a9a54656 later split server.py into mixins, cd1f0a2b9acdcad6bb1575599e2efcf5e3f66aea copied the unsafe selection into OpenAI Chat Completions and Gemini, c2451296df406bf8de4d678aa3cf1cb326738557 extended it to OpenAI Responses, and 82301bbf76679a0ff0c8fb907112be368424f932 extended it to the websocket flow; those are moves/expansions of an already-existing authorization flaw, not the root BIC.

reasoning: The authorization failure is created at the moment a network-supplied identifier becomes the persistent-memory tenant key, not when that same pattern is later copied into openai.py. da743418584725e8b9c3315dc1aea7cf5e949192 is therefore the causally minimal first-writer: it introduces the proxy memory feature, the untrusted header selection, and both read and write sinks in one public commit, and its immediate parent has none of them. The later split and provider/path additions preserve or broaden the same flaw and cannot replace the BIC. The public object is a normal one-parent commit and exposes no reconstructable squash-member history, so there is no squash decomposition to record. The landed mainline remediation is directly 1f96dabc19130947770353cd6e814db4fd96e6a0; although ac962fcce374739572c04e09269c12b9daeb457f and 839a12e0fdebe3ce44016d57a5a3590349138149 are earlier iterations on the PR branch, neither closed mainline or defines the shipped version boundary, whereas 1f96dabc19130947770353cd6e814db4fd96e6a0 is the commit first contained by v0.36.1. Finally, the audit protocol permits AI judgment only from the BIC commit object. That object has a human author/committer and no canonical AI trailer or bot identity, so later commits, PR metadata, or the code's references to LLM products cannot supply AI evidence. The closed result is therefore NOT_AI.
